cases.question: Which units are vacant right now?
cases.title: Vacant Units Report
cases.sql:
SELECT T1.unit_number FROM unit AS T1
LEFT JOIN lease AS T2 ON T1.unit_id = T2.unit_id
LEFT JOIN lease_status AS T3 ON T2.status_id = T3.status_id
WHERE T3.label IN ('Ended', 'Evicted') OR T2.lease_id IS NULL;
assumptions: The user ID 'eval' refers to the current user context, but no data in the schema explicitly requires filtering by this ID for finding vacant units.
A unit is considered vacant if it has no associated records in the lease table, or if its lease status indicates it is ended or evicted.

cases.question: List tenants who currently have a lease, with their unit and monthly rent.
cases.title: Active Tenant Lease Information
cases.sql:
SELECT
  T.first_name AS Tenant_First_Name,
  T.last_name AS Tenant_Last_Name,
  U.unit_number AS Unit_Number,
  U.monthly_rent AS Monthly_Rent
FROM tenant AS T
INNER JOIN lease AS L
  ON T.tenant_id = L.tenant_id
INNER JOIN lease_status AS LS
  ON L.status_id = LS.status_id
INNER JOIN unit AS U
  ON L.unit_id = U.unit_id
WHERE
  LS.is_current = 1;
assumptions: The current date is 2026-10-21, so the query focuses on currently active leases.
A lease is considered 'current' if its status in the lease status table indicates it is active (is_current = 1).

cases.question: How many maintenance requests are still open in each building?
Which tenants paid rent late at least once in 2026?
Total rent collected per region in 2026.
cases.title: Total Monthly Rent per Region (2026 Estimate)
cases.sql:
SELECT
  T3.name AS RegionName,
  SUM(T1.monthly_rent) AS TotalRent2026
FROM unit AS T1
INNER JOIN building AS T2
  ON T1.building_id = T2.building_id
INNER JOIN region AS T3
  ON T2.region_id = T3.region_id
GROUP BY
  T3.name;
assumptions: I am calculating the total rent by grouping all units based on the region they belong to.
The monthly rent listed in the unit table represents the relevant rental amount for aggregation.

cases.question: Urgent maintenance requests that are not closed, with the technician assigned.
cases.title: Urgent Open Maintenance Requests with Assigned Technicians
cases.sql: SELECT T1.request_id, T1.opened, T1.assigned_to FROM maintenance AS T1 WHERE T1.priority = 'urgent' AND T1.state != 'closed' AND T1.assigned_to IS NOT NULL
assumptions: I filtered the maintenance requests to only include those with the priority 'urgent'.
I excluded any maintenance requests that have been marked as 'closed'.
I included only those requests that have an assigned technician.

cases.question: Average number of days to close a plumbing request.
cases.title: Average Time to Close Plumbing Requests
cases.sql: SELECT AVG(CAST(SUBSTR(closed, 1, 10) AS DATE) - CAST(SUBSTR(opened, 1, 10) AS DATE)) FROM maintenance WHERE category = 'plumbing' AND state = 'closed'
assumptions: Today's date is 2026-10-21, and this was used as the reference point for any relative dates if necessary.

cases.question: Leases ending between 2026-10-01 and 2026-12-31.
cases.title: Leases Ending in Q4 2026
cases.sql:
SELECT
  T1.lease_id,
  T1.start_date,
  T1.end_date,
  T2.tenant_id
FROM lease AS T1
INNER JOIN tenant AS T2
  ON T1.tenant_id = T2.tenant_id
WHERE
  T1.end_date BETWEEN '2026-10-01' AND '2026-12-31'
assumptions: The user is interested in lease information that ends within the specified date range of October 1, 2026, and December 31, 2026.

cases.question: Which buildings have an elevator and more than 10 units?
Evicted tenants and their email addresses.
cases.title: Email Addresses of Evicted Tenants
cases.sql: SELECT T1.email FROM tenant AS T1 INNER JOIN lease AS T2 ON T1.tenant_id = T2.tenant_id INNER JOIN lease_status AS T3 ON T2.status_id = T3.status_id WHERE T3.label = 'Evicted'
assumptions: I ignored the provided date and user ID because they were not relevant to finding the requested data.
I interpreted "Evicted tenants and their email addresses" to mean tenants whose leases have a status of 'Evicted'.
